title: Attention kernel + KV cache rollback breadcrumbs
summary: Scratchpad for a recurring production repro where long-prefix requests occasionally produce garbled tokens after a kernel fallback / KV-cache rollback. Focus is on interaction between attention kernel selection, workspace allocation, and KV cache index alignment when sequence length crosses boundaries.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use model: llama-13b-8k (quantized q4f16) on dedicated node with GPUs: A100-80GB.
2) Start runtime with env RW_KERNEL_POLICY=auto and RW_KVCACHE_ROLLBACK=enabled.
3) Send two requests in sequence from same session: a long prompt (~3500 tokens) then a short continuation (~20 tokens) with streaming enabled.
4) Observe occasional token corruption or sudden drop to low-quality completions on the continuation.
5) Re-run with RW_KERNEL_POLICY=attn_unfused (force) and compare outputs and logs.
commands_tried:
# run trace with kernel/kvcache
RUNTIME_TRACE=kernel,kvcache python tools/run_inference.py --model llama-13b-8k --session-id s1 --input-file long_prompt.txt --stream

# force fallback path
ENV: RW_KERNEL_POLICY=attn_unfused bin/serve --config configs/dedicated-a100.json

# reproduce locally with smaller model to iterate faster
python tools/run_inference.py --model test-1b --session-id s2 --input-file long_prompt_small.txt --trace

kernel_selection_outputs: kernel_selection dump: {model=llama-13b-8k, seq_len=3500, batch=1, preferred_kernels=[flash_attn_fwd_v2, flash_attn_fwd_v1, attn_unfused], memory_estimates={flash_attn_fwd_v2:18MB, attn_unfused:6MB}}
decision: flash_attn_fwd_v2 chosen because fastest; mem_check failed at allocation time -> fallback to attn_unfused
note: attn_unfused uses different KV layout (interleaved vs contiguous) leading to different offset calculation in kv_index.c
kv_cache_observations: Observed behavior: when kernel falls back mid-session, the rollback routine triggers an evict-and-rebuild of the KV cache. Rebuild completes but the first few tokens after rebuild sometimes decode to repeated low-entropy symbols. This correlates with sessions whose prefix length crossed multiples of 2048 (e.g., 2048 -> 3500) during the long prompt. When I artificially pad the initial prompt to a fixed block size (multiple of 2048) the issue frequency drops.
hypotheses: Hypothesis A: Kernel-specific workspace alignment affects how KV cache offsets are computed; fallback leaves stale pointer arithmetic assumptions leading to off-by-N reads during first decode steps.
Hypothesis B: Rebuild routine doesn't fully reinitialize per-layer 'block_count' when seq_len > BLOCK_THRESHOLD (2048) causing early layers to read incorrect cache slices.
Hypothesis C: Quantized dtype (q4f16) + different kernel resharding causes accumulation/rounding errors in attention exp/softmax that are amplified for the first few tokens after rebuild.
Hypothesis D: Race between async KV rebuild and decode start: streaming path begins consuming tokens before all layer pointers are stable -> transient garbage tokens.
attempted_fixes: 1) Force kernel to attn_unfused at runtime (RW_KERNEL_POLICY=attn_unfused) -> corruption stops but latency + memory usage increase (~12% latency p95).
2) Add fixed-padding to prompt to next 2048 boundary (pad tokens) -> issue frequency reduced significantly in tests.
3) Serializing rebuild: introduced small sleep(25ms) after rebuild in serving runtime -> flakiness reduced but not eliminated (race may be bigger).
4) Disabled rollback (RW_ENABLE_KV_CACHE_ROLLBACK=0) causing session to continue with old KV layout -> causes immediate decode mismatch and fails more often (worse).
5) Added extra zero-initialization for per-layer pointers in rebuild routine -> local toy repro seemed to improve but production still exhibits instances.
experiment_results: Summary: pinning kernel -> elimination of corruption in ~1000-run sample but costlier. Padding appears to be a practical mitigation for customer-facing systems but not a root fix. Race-delay reduces occurrences but suggests timing window. Disabling rollback is harmful. Small changes to rebuild init look promising in toy tests; need instrumentation in prod to confirm.
next_steps:
- Add a runtime invariant check: after rebuild, compute hash of each layer KV block and assert equality with rebuild-time computed digest before allowing decode to continue. Log digest mismatches with full memory offsets.
- Instrument kernel selector to record exact workspace size/alignment and per-layer stride for both kernels.
- Create minimal C++ repro (single GPU, synthetic model with same layer count) that forces fallback during long prefix to validate Hypothesis A/B.
- Discuss trade-offs with infra: is pinning kernel for customers with heavy long-prefix workloads acceptable as fast mitigation? Prepare cost impact note.
- If race confirmed: delay decode start until all per-layer digests validated or make rebuild synchronous for affected sessions.
notes: Random incidental: one of the failing traces had a memmgr warning about alignment=512 vs expected=256; surprised because our allocator typically rounds up. Might be introduced when buffer is borrowed by attention kernel for scratchpad; follow that call chain next. Also suspect interplay with CUDA 12.3 driver changes (recent upgrade on staging) — reproduce on older driver to isolate.
